items.question: What is the never-exceed airspeed (Vne) at 2200 lb takeoff gross weight and below?
items.explanation: Section 2 AIRSPEED LIMITS specifies Vne 130 KIAS at 2200 lb TOGW and below.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: AIRSPEED LIMITS (p.2-1)

items.question: What is the never-exceed airspeed (Vne) when takeoff gross weight is over 2200 lb?
items.explanation: For TOGW over 2200 lb the POH limits Vne to 120 KIAS.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: AIRSPEED LIMITS (p.2-1)

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed in autorotation?
items.explanation: The AIRSPEED LIMITS table gives a maximum autorotation airspeed of 100 KIAS.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: AIRSPEED LIMITS (p.2-1)

items.question: With any combination of cabin doors removed, what is the maximum approved airspeed?
items.explanation: Additional airspeed limits specify 100 KIAS maximum with any combination of cabin doors removed.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: AIRSPEED LIMITS (p.2-1)

items.question: For power-on operation, what is the permitted main rotor speed range?
items.explanation: ROTOR SPEED LIMITS list a power-on rotor speed range of 101-102% NR (404-408 RPM).
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: ROTOR SPEED LIMITS (p.2-2)

items.question: For power-off rotor operation, what is the permitted rotor speed range?
items.explanation: With power off, rotor speed is limited to 90-108% NR (360-432 RPM).
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: ROTOR SPEED LIMITS (p.2-2)

items.question: When is transient operation below 101% rotor RPM permitted?
options: Only in autorotation below 500 ft AGL
items.explanation: A note under rotor speed limits allows transient operation below 101% NR only for emergency procedures training.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: ROTOR SPEED LIMITS (p.2-2)

items.question: What is the maximum continuous engine speed for the IO-540-AE1A5, expressed as a percentage of rated RPM?
items.explanation: POWERPLANT LIMITATIONS show maximum continuous engine speed of 102% (2718 RPM).
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: POWERPLANT LIMITATIONS (p.2-2)

items.question: Which combination of gross weight limits is correct for the R44 II?
items.explanation: WEIGHT LIMITS define a maximum gross weight of 2500 lb and a minimum gross weight of 1600 lb.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: WEIGHT LIMITS (p.2-3)

items.question: What is the maximum permitted weight per seat, including baggage compartment?
items.explanation: The WEIGHT LIMITS section states a maximum of 300 lb (136 kg) per seat including baggage compartment.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: WEIGHT LIMITS (p.2-3)

items.question: What is the maximum allowable load in any baggage compartment?
items.explanation: Maximum load in any baggage compartment is limited to 50 lb (23 kg).
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: WEIGHT LIMITS (p.2-3)

items.question: With all doors installed, what minimum solo pilot weight ensures the center of gravity will be within limits without adding ballast?
items.explanation: CENTER OF GRAVITY LIMITS note that a solo pilot weight of 150 lb (68 kg) or more keeps CG within limits with doors installed.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: CENTER OF GRAVITY LIMITS (p.2-3)

items.question: Are aerobatic manoeuvres permitted in the R44 II?
options: Only for training with an instructor on board
items.explanation: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS state that aerobatic flight is prohibited.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS (p.2-5)

items.question: Which manoeuvre is specifically prohibited because of the risk of catastrophic loss of lateral control in low-G conditions?
items.explanation: The FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS section specifically prohibits low-G cyclic pushovers due to loss of lateral control risk.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS (p.2-5)

items.question: According to the limitations, is flight in known icing conditions permitted?
options: Yes, if pitot heat is ON
No, flight in known icing conditions is prohibited
items.explanation: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS state that flight in known icing conditions is prohibited.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS (p.2-5)

items.question: Which combination of altitude limitations is correct for the R44 II?
options: Maximum operating density altitude 12,000 ft; maximum operating altitude 8,000 ft AGL
Maximum operating density altitude 14,000 ft; maximum operating altitude 9,000 ft AGL
Maximum operating density altitude 16,000 ft; maximum operating altitude 10,000 ft AGL
Maximum operating density altitude 10,000 ft; maximum operating altitude 14,000 ft AGL
items.explanation: The POH limits operation to a maximum density altitude of 14,000 ft and a maximum operating altitude of 9,000 ft AGL.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS (p.2-5)

items.question: Which kinds of operation are approved for the R44 II under the POH?
options: Day and night VFR and IFR
items.explanation: KINDS OF OPERATION LIMITATIONS approve the R44 II for day and night VFR operations.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: KINDS OF OPERATION LIMITATIONS (p.2-6)

items.question: For solo flight, where must the pilot be seated according to the flight crew limitations?
items.explanation: Minimum flight crew is one pilot in the right front seat; solo flight is from the right front seat.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: FLIGHT CREW LIMITATIONS (p.2-5)

items.question: Which group of systems must be operational for dispatch according to the limitations?
options: Alternator, RPM governor, low rotor RPM warning system, OAT gage, and hydraulic control system
Alternator, pitot heat, GPS, and autopilot
Hydraulic system, anti-ice system, and flight director only
Only the rotor brake and low fuel warning system
items.explanation: The FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS list the alternator, RPM governor, low rotor RPM warning system, OAT gage, and hydraulic control system as required for dispatch.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: FLIGHT AND MANEUVER LIMITATIONS (p.2-5)

items.question: With fuel tanks equipped with bladders, what is the combined usable fuel capacity?
items.explanation: FUEL LIMITATIONS state that with bladder tanks usable capacity is 29.5 and 17.0 US gal, for a combined usable fuel of 46.5 US gal (176 liters).
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: FUEL LIMITATIONS (p.2-6)

items.question: What is the green arc range for oil pressure during flight?
items.explanation: The OIL PRESSURE instrument markings specify a green arc from 55 to 95 psi during normal operation.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: INSTRUMENT MARKINGS – OIL PRESSURE (p.2-7)

items.question: At what oil pressure does the upper red line (maximum) occur?
items.explanation: OIL PRESSURE markings show an upper red line at 115 psi.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: INSTRUMENT MARKINGS – OIL PRESSURE (p.2-7)

items.question: What is the green arc range for oil temperature?
items.explanation: OIL TEMPERATURE instrument markings specify a green arc from 75 to 245°F (24 to 118°C).
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: INSTRUMENT MARKINGS – OIL TEMPERATURE (p.2-7)

items.question: What is the maximum oil temperature allowed, corresponding to the red line?
items.explanation: OIL TEMPERATURE markings show a red line at 245°F (118°C).
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: INSTRUMENT MARKINGS – OIL TEMPERATURE (p.2-7)

items.question: What is the green arc range for cylinder head temperature (CHT)?
items.explanation: CYLINDER HEAD TEMPERATURE markings show a green arc from 200 to 500°F (93 to 260°C).
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: INSTRUMENT MARKINGS – CHT (p.2-8)

items.question: At what cylinder head temperature does the red line (maximum) occur?
items.explanation: The CHT gauge has a red line at 500°F (260°C).
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: INSTRUMENT MARKINGS – CHT (p.2-8)

items.question: What is the green arc range for manifold pressure (MAP) on the gauge?
items.explanation: MANIFOLD PRESSURE markings list a green arc from 15.0 to 23.3 inches Hg.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: INSTRUMENT MARKINGS – MANIFOLD PRESSURE (p.2-8)

items.question: Where is the manifold pressure red line located?
items.explanation: The manifold pressure gauge has a red line at 26.1 in. Hg.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: INSTRUMENT MARKINGS – MANIFOLD PRESSURE (p.2-8)

items.question: What does the yellow arc on the manifold pressure gauge represent?
options: Prohibited range due to structural resonance
Variable manifold pressure limits that depend on a placard schedule
items.explanation: The POH notes that the manifold pressure yellow arc denotes variable MAP limits and refers to a placard on page 2-9.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: INSTRUMENT MARKINGS – MANIFOLD PRESSURE (p.2-8)

items.question: Which combination correctly describes the main fuel tank usable capacity for bladder-style tanks, as shown on the placard near the main tank gauge?
items.explanation: A placard near the main tank fuel gauge for bladder-style tanks states 29.5 US gallons usable.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: PLACARDS – MAIN FUEL TANK (p.2-10)

items.question: For bladder-style tanks, what usable capacity is shown on the placard near the auxiliary fuel tank gauge?
items.explanation: The auxiliary tank fuel gauge placard for bladder-style tanks shows AUX 17.0 US GAL.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: PLACARDS – AUX FUEL TANK (p.2-11)

items.question: According to the baggage compartment placard, what is the maximum weight allowed in each baggage compartment?
items.explanation: The baggage compartment placard states COMPARTMENT CAPACITY: 50 LB MAX.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: PLACARDS – BAGGAGE COMPARTMENT (p.2-12)

items.question: What combined weight limit is given on the baggage compartment placard for seat plus compartment?
items.explanation: The placard cautions not to exceed 300 lb combined seat plus compartment.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: PLACARDS – BAGGAGE COMPARTMENT (p.2-12)

items.question: What does the NO SMOKING placard require for all occupants?
options: Smoking permitted only with windows open
Smoking prohibited in flight but allowed on ground
No smoking at any time in the cabin
items.explanation: A placard in clear view of all occupants states NO SMOKING, implying no smoking at any time in the cabin.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: PLACARDS – NO SMOKING (p.2-11)

items.question: What does the red color in the instrument marking color code indicate?
options: Operating limit that must not be exceeded in normal operation
items.explanation: The COLOR CODE FOR INSTRUMENT MARKINGS defines red as operating limit; the pointer should not enter red during normal operation.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: COLOR CODE FOR INSTRUMENT MARKINGS (p.2-1)

items.question: What does the green color in the instrument marking color code indicate?
items.explanation: The color code describes green as the normal operating range.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: COLOR CODE FOR INSTRUMENT MARKINGS (p.2-1)

items.question: On the airspeed indicator, what is the green arc range?
items.explanation: The AIRSPEED INDICATOR instrument markings specify a green arc from 0 to 110 KIAS.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: INSTRUMENT MARKINGS – AIRSPEED INDICATOR (p.2-7)

items.question: What does the yellow arc on the airspeed indicator represent?
options: Precautionary range where special operating procedures apply
items.explanation: The color code defines yellow as the precautionary or special operating procedure range; on the airspeed indicator this is 110–130 KIAS.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: COLOR CODE / AIRSPEED INDICATOR (p.2-1, p.2-7)

items.question: What special placard must be installed near earlier airspeed indicators that do not have a yellow arc?
options: DO NOT EXCEED 100 KIAS IN TURBULENCE
DO NOT EXCEED 110 KIAS EXCEPT IN SMOOTH AIR
DO NOT EXCEED 120 KIAS BELOW 1000 FT AGL
DO NOT EXCEED 130 KIAS WITH PASSENGERS
items.explanation: For earlier airspeed indicators without a yellow arc, a placard adjacent to the indicator must state: DO NOT EXCEED 110 KIAS EXCEPT IN SMOOTH AIR.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: INSTRUMENT MARKINGS – AIRSPEED INDICATOR (p.2-7)

items.question: What is the green arc range on the rotor tachometer?
items.explanation: The ROTOR TACHOMETER instrument markings show a green arc from 90 to 108%.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: INSTRUMENT MARKINGS – ROTOR TACHOMETER (p.2-7)

items.question: Where are the lower and upper red lines on the rotor tachometer scale?
items.explanation: ROTOR TACHOMETER markings specify a lower red line at 90% and an upper red line at 108%.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: INSTRUMENT MARKINGS – ROTOR TACHOMETER (p.2-7)

items.question: On the engine tachometer, what is the green arc range?
items.explanation: The ENGINE TACHOMETER markings show a green arc from 101 to 102%.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: INSTRUMENT MARKINGS – ENGINE TACHOMETER (p.2-7)

items.question: What are the lower and upper red lines on the engine tachometer?
options: Lower 101%, upper 102% with short-time operation above
items.explanation: ENGINE TACHOMETER markings list a lower red line at 101% and an upper red line at 102%.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: INSTRUMENT MARKINGS – ENGINE TACHOMETER (p.2-7)

items.question: What is the lower red line value on the oil pressure gauge?
items.explanation: OIL PRESSURE instrument markings specify a lower red line at 25 psi.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: INSTRUMENT MARKINGS – OIL PRESSURE (p.2-7)

items.question: What is the lower yellow arc range on the oil pressure gauge?
items.explanation: The OIL PRESSURE gauge has a lower yellow arc from 25 to 55 psi.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: INSTRUMENT MARKINGS – OIL PRESSURE (p.2-7)

items.question: What is the upper yellow arc range on the oil pressure gauge?
items.explanation: OIL PRESSURE markings show an upper yellow arc from 95 to 115 psi.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: INSTRUMENT MARKINGS – OIL PRESSURE (p.2-7)

items.question: According to the fuel limitations table, what is the combined total fuel capacity (tanks with bladders) in US gallons?
items.explanation: The FUEL CAPACITY table lists a combined total capacity of 47.7 US gallons for tanks with bladders.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: FUEL LIMITATIONS – FUEL CAPACITY (p.2-6)

items.question: For tanks without bladders, what is the combined usable fuel capacity in US gallons?
items.explanation: The FUEL CAPACITY table shows a combined usable capacity of 48.9 US gallons for tanks without bladders.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: FUEL LIMITATIONS – FUEL CAPACITY (p.2-6)

items.question: Which statement about fuel tanks without bladders is correct according to the limitations note?
options: They are preferred due to higher capacity
They may be used only in day VFR
They should no longer be in service per R44 Service Bulletin SB-78B
They may be used only with reduced gross weight
items.explanation: A note in the FUEL LIMITATIONS section states that fuel tanks without bladders should no longer be in service, per R44 Service Bulletin SB-78B.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: FUEL LIMITATIONS – NOTE (p.2-6)

items.question: According to the KINDS OF OPERATION LIMITATIONS, what is required for night VFR flight?
options: Only landing lights must be operable
Landing, navigation, instrument, and anti-collision lights must be operational
Only navigation and anti-collision lights must be operational
No specific lighting requirements are stated
items.explanation: KINDS OF OPERATION LIMITATIONS specify that night VFR operation is permitted only when landing, navigation, instrument, and anti-collision lights are operational.
references: R44 II POH Sec 2: KINDS OF OPERATION LIMITATIONS (p.2-6)
